comparison: Perfect agreement on C1-C3. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept that MPS1 inhibition successfully induces CIN, with converging evidence from multiple assays. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Agreement on C4-C6. Both accept the bulk RNA-sequencing findings from whole tumors. OpenEval notes the limitation of n=2 tumors per condition, while peer reviewers do not raise concerns about these data.

Strong agreement on C7-C8. Both evaluations support the conditioned media experiment showing M1 polarization. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight this as 'the most compelling experiment,' while OpenEval finds the clustering analysis and marker expression patterns convincing.
Agreement on C9-C10. Both accept the flow cytometry validation of M1 polarization in 3D tumoroids. Peer review R4 also covers C11-C12, which OpenEval addresses separately in R5.
Agreement on C11-C12. Both accept the cell size increase and decreased Tyrp1 binding findings. Peer review groups these with C9-C10 in a single result, while OpenEval separates them.
Agreement on C13-C14. Both accept the 3D tumoroid phagocytosis assay results showing differential responses based on CIN status and opsonization. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Agreement on C15-C19. Both accept the in vivo immune infiltration data showing increased macrophages and other immune cells. Findings are consistent with the overall narrative accepted by both evaluations.
Agreement on C20-C22. Both accept the baseline control findings establishing that neither CD47 KO alone nor anti-Tyrp1 alone is sufficient for tumor rejection. No concerns raised.

Strong agreement on C23-C25. Both evaluations explicitly highlight the impressive 97% survival rate with combination therapy. Peer reviewers call this 'a striking improvement,' while OpenEval notes the remarkably high survival rate and substantial sample sizes.

Agreement on C26-C28. Both accept the adoptive transfer experiments demonstrating macrophages as key effector cells. Peer reviewers explicitly mention adoptively transferred macrophages as part of impressive survival rates.
Agreement on C29-C31. Both accept the antibody response data showing IgG generation and epitope spreading. No concerns raised about these findings.
Agreement on C32-C34. Both accept the functional validation of IgG pro-phagocytic activity. Peer review R11 also covers C35, which OpenEval addresses in R13.
Agreement on C35. Both accept the comparable efficacy of sera to anti-Tyrp1 monoclonal antibody in 3D tumoroids. OpenEval also addresses C36 in this result, which peer review covers in R12.
Agreement on C36. Both accept the in vivo pre-opsonization experiments. Peer review R12 also covers C37-C39, which OpenEval addresses separately in R14.
Agreement on C37-C39. Both accept the second challenge survival data showing differential protective immunity against CIN versus non-CIN tumors. No concerns raised.
Agreement on C40-C43. Both accept the immune memory data from second challenge tumors showing enhanced cell-mediated immunity. No concerns raised about these findings.
Agreement on C44. Both accept the third challenge survival data demonstrating durable acquired immunity. No concerns raised.

Agreement on C45-C47. Both accept the NSG versus C57BL/6 comparison data and the conclusion about macrophages being key effector cells. OpenEval suggests additional depletion experiments would strengthen C47, while peer reviewers do not raise this concern.

Strong agreement on C48-C49. Both evaluations explicitly praise the impressive survival rates and accept the overall conclusion about CIN creating vulnerabilities for macrophage attack. This represents the central thesis accepted by both.

Partial disagreement on C50-C52. OpenEval finds these mechanistic synthesis claims well-supported, noting they represent reasonable inferences that could benefit from additional studies. Peer reviewers rate this as UNCERTAIN, raising a critical caveat that effects may be due to MSP1 inhibition specifically rather than CIN more generally, affecting mechanism attribution.

OpenEval evaluates C53-C55 (literature context about CIN and immune evasion) as supported, noting these claims appropriately distinguish between late-stage highly aneuploid tumors and early-stage CIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates C56-C58 (established background on calreticulin, CD47, and 'don't eat me' signals) as supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates C59-C62 (clinical and experimental context including CD47-targeting trials and CIN effects) as supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
